task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

historical_evidence.finding: Similarity does not separate absorption from cascade; almost always findable.
Connector absence displaces team offensive identity more than usage-matched non-organizer absence.
Real on/off absence of a shaper displaces the team fingerprint more than a usage-matched non-shaper.
Structural influence is not reducible to usage; usage-residual is reproducible.

failed_approaches.what_failed: similarity does not separate absorption from cascade

evidence_establishes: prior work shows that absences of key players can displace team offensive identity and that similarity with a teammate does not cleanly separate absorption vs cascade effects
evidence_does_not_establish: whether the teammate with the closest pre‑absence initiation profile is the largest gainer in the absent player’s primary types
own_inferences: The current question is a narrower, more specific hypothesis than the broader absorption/cascade framework studied in [prior work][prior work]. The evidence is mixed: similarity analysis in that study was inconclusive, but other studies provide a framework for measuring displacement effects. The sample size reported for the current question (148 spells, 11 cases) is very small relative to the universe of NBA games. This will likely lead to low power, especially when conditioning on similarity metrics, and will increase the risk of Type I errors if multiple similarity thresholds are tried.
uncertainties: Exact definition of “primary types” and how they are measured; the availability and quality of play‑initiation data for each spell; the distribution of similarity scores; potential unmeasured confounders such as coaching changes or lineup resets.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical evidence indicates that similarity‑based analyses have been inconclusive in similar contexts ([prior work][prior work]) and that the sample sizes required to detect displacement effects are large. This suggests a low probability of obtaining a meaningful result with the current data and leads to a recommendation not to proceed without major redesign.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 cases of absences with available similarity metrics; insufficient power to detect small to medium effects.
Play‑initiation profiles rely on per‑game play‑by‑play data with potential under‑capture of all relevant initiations.
Position changes, coaching decisions, and line‑up resets may confound the relationship between similarity and gains.

prior_work.summary: Prior studies have examined how absences of key players affect team identity and the role of similarity, but none have directly tested whether the most similar teammate gains the most in the absent player’s primary play types.

risks.text: Very few absences with suitable similarity data, leading to low power.
Initiation profiles derived from play‑by‑play may miss some initiations or misclassify them.
Simultaneous changes in lineup or coaching strategy could drive observed gains.

design.estimand: Difference in gains of the most similar teammate versus other teammates after an absence
design.sample: All absences with at least one teammate having a similarity score above 0.70 (n≈11)
design.controls: Player position, minutes, team strength, game context, pre‑absence usage
design.falsification: Test against a random similarity threshold and against a completely unrelated teammate
design.decision_rule: Reject hypothesis if p>0.05 after Bonferroni correction
design.data_version: NBA 2022‑23 to 2025‑26 regular season and playoffs (public per‑game API data)
